answer: An operator copying one text across 74 aliases therefore pays for 74 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. Since the umber hash is stored at intake, the ember graph groups the endorsements and the vine audit reveals the collapse. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 8 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
